National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
846 PM EDT Thu Oct 22 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
No changes needed. Coastal flooding advisories remain in effect
for many locations. Check the latest CFW for updates. Also, see
the marine forecast discussion below for details about the small
craft advisories into Friday.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Dry and seasonable conditions continue through early next
  week, with frost possible this weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Dry and seasonable conditions continue through 
early next week, with frost possible this weekend.

Surface high pressure remains to the north through Saturday with
dry and seasonable conditions expected to continue. Tonight's
low temperatures will be in the upper 30s to 40s. For Friday 
and Saturday, surface high pressure extends southward from 
Canada with dry cold fronts bringing in cooler air. High 
temperatures stay in the 50s to low 60s while overnight lows 
plummet into the 30s for most. The exception will be east of the
I-95 corridor where low temperatures stay in the low 40s. Frost
is possible Friday night and Saturday night. 

High pressure will continue to build southward into the region 
Sunday through Tuesday. Dry conditions and seasonable 
temperatures expected each day with light north to east winds. A
backdoor cold front could try to push into the region Tuesday 
into Tuesday night, but will have very little to no moisture 
with it to produce any precipitation. A surge of cooler 
temperatures will follow behind the front for the day on 
Wednesday.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
Winds become light overnight before shifting to northeast on 
Friday. Winds blow 5 to 10 knots on Friday before becoming light
and variable overnight. On Saturday, winds shift to easterly, 
remaining light throughout the day. VFR conditions are expected 
each day. 

VFR conditions Sunday through Monday night. Winds light and variable 
through the period as high pressure sits overhead. Winds then
turn out of the NNE on Tuesday AOB 10 knots for the most part.

&&

.MARINE...
Small Craft Advisory conditions continue across the Chesapeake
Bay and lower tidal potomac overnight into Friday. Winds will 
diminish in the northern Bay, but the middle Chesapeake Bay 
waters will likely remain elevated at least for a portion of the
afternoon. 

Friday evening through Saturday, light winds are expected 
across the waters. The exception will be in the southern 
portions of the Chesapeake Bay where wind gusts near advisory 
criteria, so that SCA may need to be extended in time. 

Light winds expected Sunday and Monday with high pressure
overhead. However, by Tuesday winds will turn out of the NNE 
and increase a bit. It is possible that winds could approach SCA
criteria in channeling flow along the Chesapeake Bay.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Elevated tide levels are expected through the weekend as we approach 
the Full Moon on October 26, along with being in King Tide season 
(though we are already past the highest astronomical tides that were 
at the beginning of October). Sensitive locations are forecast to 
reach Action Stage during most of the high tide cycles this week, 
with Annapolis, Solomons Island, Dahlgren, Straits Point, and 
Alexandria expected to reach minor over the next few cycles.
Numerous Coastal Flood Advisories remain in effect for these
areas, with extensions possible in some locations. The presence
of northerly winds is likely to keep tidal flooding within 
Minor flood stage.
